mla_facts.statement: A decoder entry is DSA exactly when compress_ratios[entry] <= 0 (the pinned config uses -2) and the entry index is below len(compress_ratios); the model builder is Ernie5_5DecoderLayer, which builds Ernie5_5DSAAttention for such an entry and the HCA class for every other. The six main MLA layers are therefore 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 (zero based) and the separate draft entry 43 (index num_hidden_layers + 0) is also DSA because its ratio is -2.

The trailing window width is config.sliding_window (pinned: 128). It is read once as self.window and handed to merge_swa_topk and to the indexer metadata builder; both DSA and HCA layers use the same value.

Exact window endpoints. For the query at position p let seq = p + 1. merge_swa_topk writes the window as token indices seq-w .. seq-1 INCLUSIVE with w = min(seq, window): for window 128 the window is positions p-127 .. p, 128 tokens, and the query's own token is its last entry (the first full window is at seq = 128: [0, 127]; at seq = 129 it is [1, 128]). Request-local absolute indices are used, not page slots.

The indexer scores only tokens OLDER than the window: candidates are the half-open range [0, max(seq - window, 0)). Prefill clamps the per-row exclusive end cu_seqlen_ke to max(ke - window, ks); decode subtracts the window from seq_lens and clamps at 0. The unwindowed exclusive end for DSA (compress ratio 1) is pos + 1, so the windowed end is pos + 1 - window = window_start. Candidates and window are disjoint and together cover [0, seq) whenever the indexer is not truncated by top-k. The torch reference of the logits masks keys with ks <= j < ke (ke exclusive).

Selected-candidate count n = min(max(seq - window, 0), index_topk) (pinned index_topk 2048); the merged row is [indexer top-k ids (first n entries) | window ids ascending | -1 padding], width index_topk + sliding_window = 2176. The kernel masks every indexer slot at or beyond n, so unspecified tail contents never matter. Truncation first happens at seq = window + index_topk + 1 = 2177.

mla_facts.statement: The ORDER of the indexer's selected ids inside the first n slots and the tie-breaking between equal scores are decided by the top_k_per_row kernels (prefill and decode), which are CUDA/ROCm kernels outside the pinned Python. Attention is invariant to the order of its candidates up to floating-point summation order, so only tie handling at the k-th boundary can change the selected SET.

resolver.action: Read csrc top_k_per_row_prefill / top_k_per_row_decode at vLLM v0.32.0 (csrc/sampler.cu or its includes) for tie order and for what fills slots beyond the valid count, then pin the answer with a tied-score fixture in story 3-1.

mla_facts.why: The selection and tie kernels (top_k_per_row_prefill/decode) are compiled ops; their source was not part of the pinned Python read.
mla_facts.impact: A CPU selection op could pick a different set than the reference when scores tie at the k-th place.

mla_facts.statement: Causality holds by construction: every window index is <= p and every indexer candidate is < seq - window <= p, so no future token and no uninitialised page can be selected; with seq <= window the indexer range is empty and the row is the window alone. The window and the candidate range never overlap, so no token is attended twice in a DSA layer (contrast the HCA overlap in h08).

Main-path positional split: q is [qk_nope_head_dim | qk_rope_head_dim] per head (192 | 64) and RoPE is applied to the TRAILING slice q[..., nope:]; k_pe is the trailing 64 of the fused qkv_a projection (a single head shared by all heads) rotated separately and cached after the normed latent. The rotary is GPT-J interleaved (is_neox_style=False), plain default RoPE at rope_theta (pinned 8,000,000), with NO YaRN scaling: YaRN applies to HCA layers only. Table precision (corrected in story 3-2b): the DSA layers use the DEFAULT RotaryEmbedding, which builds its cos/sin table from f32 angles and then casts the whole table to the model dtype (bf16 here: get_rope takes torch.get_default_dtype() and base.py casts `cache.to(dtype)`), so the served model rotates with BF16 cos and sin; the f32 cos/sin cache of deepseek_scaling_rope.py belongs to the HCA YaRN class only.

mla_facts.statement: Indexer positional order differs from the main path: its q (64 heads x 128) is split ROPE FIRST, [rope 64 | nope 64], rotated NeoX split-half (is_neox_style=True) with the same plain rope_theta RoPE, concatenated back as [rotated | nope] and only then Hadamard-transformed over the whole 128. k comes from wk_weights_proj, passes LayerNorm(128, eps 1e-6) (weight and bias) BEFORE the rope split, gets the same transforms, and the per-head weights are the tail n_head columns of the same projection.

Indexer scoring: q is quantised per token-group of 128 to FP8 E4M3 with a power-of-two (UE8M0) scale; the head weights are multiplied by that scale and by weights_scale = head_dim^-0.5 * n_head^-0.5 (the Hadamard is orthonormal, so only this scaling is folded); the logit of key j is sum over heads of relu(q_h . k_j * k_scale_j) * weight_h, with k stored as FP8 plus an fp32 scale. The ROCm torch fallback pinned in v0.32.0 is the readable statement of the arithmetic.

Softmax scale is qk_head_dim^-0.5 with qk_head_dim = qk_nope + qk_rope = 192 + 64 = 256 (0.0625 for the pinned config), passed to the sparse MLA layer; there is no YaRN magnitude or mscale factor on the DSA path.

mla_facts.statement: Attention is absorbed latent MQA for decode AND prefill (sparse_mla_force_mqa is forced on): q_nope is absorbed by W_UK, scores are taken against the 576-wide latent row, the value is the latent and the result is expanded by W_UV. kv_b_proj is [W_UK ; W_UV] concatenated per head, i.e. per head 192 key rows then 256 value rows (28672 rows for 64 heads), so key and value head widths are NOT equal.

mla_facts.statement: KV layout: one latent row per token = RMS-normed kv_c (512) followed by the rotated k_pe (64), 576 elements, a single KV head, in 64-token pages (DSA_BLOCK_SIZE). A bf16 row is 1152 bytes; the fp8_ds_mla row is 656 bytes: 512 FP8 values, 4 fp32 scales (one per 128), then 64 bf16 rope values. The indexer has its own key cache, one row per TOKEN (compress ratio 1): 128 FP8 values plus one fp32 scale = 132 bytes (MXFP4: 64 packed bytes + 4 UE8M0 scales = 68), also 64-token pages.

mla_facts.statement: The cache dtype is a serving choice, not a model property: the DSA layer needs the sink-capable FLASHMLA_SPARSE backend and validates the configured kv_cache_dtype against it; that backend's table accepts auto, bfloat16, fp8_ds_mla (fp8 is an alias) and nvfp4_ds_mla (SM100 only); the indexer cache is always uint8 (FP8 or MXFP4 pages). Radiance must pick its own cache dtype; neither the config nor the checkpoint fixes it.

Attention sink: a learned per-head fp32 logit (attn_sink, one value per local head; checkpoint tensor core_attention.softmax_offset, BF16 [64], renamed by the weight mapper) that joins each head's softmax as ONE extra logit with NO value: the running max includes it and exp(sink - max) is added to the denominator only; the numerator is still the keys' weighted values. Heads padded for the kernel get -inf (a no-op). The sink therefore enters each (query token, head) softmax exactly once.

provenance.quote: The kernels fold the sink into the softmax denominator.

mla_facts.statement: Output order for a DSA layer: attention output o [tokens, heads, v_head_dim 256] -> VHA head mix -> times sigmoid(gate) element by element (gate = o_gate(q_c) with q_c the q_a_layernorm OUTPUT, width heads x v_head_dim = 16384) -> wo_b (16384 -> 4096). The gate multiplies AFTER the VHA mix and BEFORE the output projection.

VHA (value-head mixing): o[h] <- sum_g m[h,g] o[g] with m = I + V U^T, U and V [heads, 16] (rank 16), acting on the HEAD axis independently for each token and each of the v_head_dim columns. With tp = 1 the heads x heads matrix m is folded once from U and V and applied as one matmul on the [tokens, heads, dim] attention output. The checkpoint carries vha_postmix_U and vha_postmix_V as BF16 [64, 16].

provenance.quote: ``o[h] <- sum_g m[h, g] * o[g]`` with ``m = I + V @ U^T``.

mla_facts.statement: The dtype and rounding of the folded VHA matrix m: it is built with addmm in the parameter dtype and copied into a buffer created with torch.eye(num_heads) under whatever default dtype is active when the layer is constructed; whether m is bf16-rounded (as the loader's dtype context suggests) or kept in fp32 cannot be proven from the pinned Python alone.

mla_facts.statement: There is no per-head q/k RMS norm on the DSA path (the config flags use_qk_norm and qk_norm_type are not referenced by the pinned code, and layers 7 and 43 carry no per-head norm tensors): the only norms are q_a_layernorm (RMSNorm 1024), kv_a_layernorm (RMSNorm 512) and the indexer's LayerNorm, all with eps = rms_norm_eps except the indexer's fixed 1e-6. Many config flags (use_gated_attn, use_vha_attention, add_full_attention_sink_bias, gated_attn_act, use_fast_hadamard, rope_interleave, qk_pos_emb_head_dim, hca_rope_type, ...) are not referenced anywhere in the 14 non-parser files of the pinned src/vllm_ernie (grep, zero hits): gate, VHA and sink are unconditional in the pinned code, so Radiance must not branch on them.

Tensor geometry of a DSA entry (identical for layers 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 and the draft entry 43, checked for all seven entries against the real shard headers): q_a_proj [1024,4096] and kv_a_proj_with_mqa [576,4096] feed one fused projection; q_b_proj [16384,1024] (64 heads x 256); kv_b_proj [28672,512]; o_gate (gate_proj) [16384,1024]; o_proj [4096,16384]; indexer wq_b [8192,1024] FP8, wk [128,4096] and weights_proj [64,4096] BF16 (not quantised), k_norm weight and bias [128]; softmax_offset [64]; vha U and V [64,16]. Block-FP8 weights carry weight_scale_inv [ceil(rows/128), ceil(cols/128)].

Precision boundaries on the DSA path: activations and attention output are model dtype (bf16); the sigmoid gate is taken in model dtype; sink is fp32; indexer q is FP8 E4M3 with a power-of-two scale, its weights fp32 after scaling, its keys FP8 plus fp32 scale, logits fp32; the Hadamard runs on bf16 rows (the pinned comment calls it orthonormal); the latent cache is bf16 or fp8_ds_mla by serving choice. QKV and output projections are block-FP8 (128x128) weights with dynamic activation quantisation in the reference runtime.

mla_facts.statement: MXFP4 indexer eligibility: the indexer uses an MXFP4 key cache when dsa_indexer_uses_fp4(vllm_config) holds (a serving option), and its constructor then refuses any prefill or decode context parallelism (PCP and DCP must both be 1). The FP8 indexer cache (132 bytes a token) has no such restriction; initial parity should use it.

hca_facts.statement: Every non-DSA entry is an HCA layer: its compression ratio is max(1, compress_ratios[layer]) = 128 for the 37 main layers (all entries below num_hidden_layers except the six DSA ones). The ratio-4 'C4A' variant (with overlap and a lightning indexer) exists in the DeepSeek-V4 code but is never selected by this checkpoint: only ratios 128 and -2 occur, and compress_ratio == 128 builds no indexer. A draft entry whose ratio were 128 would get compress_ratio 1 (SWA only) because the index is not below num_hidden_layers; the pinned checkpoint's draft entry is -2 so this does not arise.

HCA window endpoints equal the DSA ones: the SWA kernel starts at max(pos - (window - 1), 0) and ends at pos + 1 EXCLUSIVE (right visibility is 0 for text), i.e. positions p-127 .. p inclusive for window 128, the query token included; the prefill combine kernel uses the same swa_start and swa_len = pos - swa_start + 1. The cached window is a separate 64-token-page SWA cache.

Compressed candidates of a query at position p are entries 0 .. (p+1)//128 - 1, i.e. only COMPLETE groups (group j covers tokens 128j .. 128j+127 and is visible once p >= 128j + 127); the count is min((p+1)//ratio, width) and the list is [0..n-1] followed by -1 padding. The sparse list is NOT limited by index_topk 2048 (no indexer at ratio 128): its width is the next power of two (at least 128) above max_seq_len // 128, bounded by cdiv(max_model_len,128) rounded up to 128.

One softmax runs over the UNION of the window keys and the compressed keys (plus the sink): prefill builds a combined index list [compressed 0..n-1 | window] and calls one sparse forward with topk_length = n + window length; decode passes the window as the main cache and the compressed rows as the extra cache of one call. The union is not de-duplicated: combined_len = topk_len + swa_len. The bf16 FlashInfer path builds the same union as one index matrix, the SWA slot ids first and the compressed slot ids after them, with one active length per token; its kernel was not read.

hca_facts.statement: A compressed entry is produced at the LAST token of its group: the compress step is skipped unless (position + 1) % ratio == 0. At that token the window of the previous ratio states (position - 127 .. position, no overlap lane because overlap is only for ratio 4: coff = 1 + overlap = 1) is pooled. Every token, complete group or not, first stores its raw kv (fp32) and score + APE[position % ratio] (fp32) in the state cache.

hca_facts.statement: Compression arithmetic of one group: per CHANNEL (not per row) softmax over the 128 rows of (score + APE) in fp32, the softmax-weighted sum of the 128 fp32 kv rows, then an fp32 RMSNorm over all 512 dims with the compressor's own weight (eps rms_norm_eps), then the split: the first 448 (nope) dims are rounded to bf16 and quantised to FP8 E4M3 in blocks of 64 with UE8M0 scales, the trailing 64 (rope) dims are GPT-J rotated from the un-rounded fp32 value and stored as bf16. With a non-uint8 (bf16 / per-tensor fp8) cache the compressor is told to store the full row (store_full_kv) instead of the packed fp8_ds_mla layout; the exact arithmetic of that CUDA path is part of the open item h21.

hca_facts.statement: The incomplete trailing group (tokens after the last multiple of 128, at most 127 of them) exists only in the fp32 partial-state cache and is INVISIBLE as a compressed entry; it is covered by the window alone, which is always at least as long as the incomplete group (window 128 >= ratio - 1 = 127), so every token is attended either raw (window) or through a complete compressed entry. The state persists across chunked-prefill steps; _get_c128_boundary reports a chunk as completing a group when start % 128 + chunk_len >= 128.

The window and the most recent complete group OVERLAP: tokens in both are attended raw (window) and again inside the compressed entry. The pinned source performs no exclusion or de-duplication (the combined length is the plain sum), so a faithful implementation must keep the duplicate; the overlap is max(0, 128 * complete_groups - window_start) tokens: 128 (the whole window) at the token that completes a group, then one fewer per further token (127 at the next token) until the next group completes.

HCA softmax scale is head_dim^-0.5 = 512^-0.5 (not the DSA 256^-0.5), passed to the sparse forward as softmax_scale / sm_scale; keys and values are the SAME single 512-wide row (multi-query, K = V), so the attention output per head is 512 wide.

HCA positional transforms: q (64 heads x 512) gets a weightless per-head RMSNorm over all 512 dims (eps rms_norm_eps) and then GPT-J interleaved RoPE on the TRAILING 64 dims (pairs (448+2i, 448+2i+1): even' = e cos - o sin, odd' = e sin + o cos); kv is first RMS-normed with kv_norm, then rotated the same way on its trailing 64 dims at its own position before it enters the SWA cache. Because V is the rotated K row, the attention output carries position dependence in its trailing 64 dims, and the output projection applies the INVERSE rotation (sin negated) at the query position before wo_a.

The frequency blend is inv = interp (1 - mask) + extrap mask with mask = 1 - ramp over the correction range [floor(dim(beta_fast)), ceil(dim(beta_slow))] clamped to [0, dim-1], computed from the ORIGINAL max position; the cos/sin cache is fp32 with original_max x factor rows.

hca_facts.statement: KV layout and pages: the compressed cache holds one row per group (tokens_per_state = 128) in the cache's page structure with block_size // 128 compressed rows per page; the fp8_ds_mla row is 584 bytes (448 FP8 nope | 64 bf16 rope = 128 bytes | 8 scale bytes = 7 UE8M0 + 1 pad, all data rows of a page first and its scale rows after), alignment 576; the bf16 FlashInfer row is 512 bf16 = 1024 bytes. hca_facts.statement: HCA cache dtype is selected by the serving kv_cache_dtype exactly as for DSA: bf16/auto -> plain bf16 rows (FlashInfer TRTLLM-gen sparse MLA), fp8 -> fp8_ds_mla with UE8M0 block scales (FlashMLA); per-tensor FP8 plain rows also exist in the DeepSeek code. The compressor STATE is always fp32 regardless of the cache dtype.

Compressor state per request and HCA layer: one row per recent token holding kv (512 fp32) and score (512 fp32) = 1024 floats = 4096 bytes, kept for a sliding window of coff * ratio = 128 rows in 8-row state blocks that share physical pages with the KV blocks; the APE parameter is fp32 [128, 512]. The state rows of the current incomplete group (and, until the group completes, all of its 128 rows) must survive across steps and chunks; rows older than 128 tokens are never read.

Output order for an HCA layer: attention output (512-wide heads, padded to 64 heads) -> VHA head mix (acting on the head axis, hence it commutes with the dim-axis inverse RoPE and runs before it) -> inverse RoPE on the trailing 64 dims at the query position and the GROUPED wo_a (8 groups of 8 heads: 4096 -> o_lora_rank 1024 each) -> times sigmoid(gate) element by element (gate = o_gate(q_norm output), width n_groups x o_lora_rank = 8192) -> wo_b (8192 -> 4096). So the HCA gate multiplies the wo_a output, not the attention output.

hca_facts.statement: HCA attention sink: a per-head fp32 parameter initialised to -inf (padded to 64 heads) and filled from the checkpoint tensor core_attention.attn_sink (F32 [64]); semantics are identical to the DSA sink (extra logit, no value, denominator only) and it joins the same single softmax over window plus compressed keys.
VHA on HCA layers is the same module as on DSA (m = I + V U^T, rank 16, U and V BF16 [64,16]) but acts on 512-wide heads; with tp = 1 it is one matmul with the folded 64 x 64 matrix.

Tensor geometry of an HCA layer (identical for all 37 layers, checked against the real shard headers): q_down [1024,4096] and kv [512,4096] feed one fused projection; q_up [32768,1024] (64 x 512); o_group (wo_a) [8192,4096] FP8 with weight_scale_inv [64,32]; o_proj [4096,8192]; gate_proj [8192,1024]; compressor linear_wkv and linear_wgate [512,4096] BF16 (plain, unquantised), ape [128,512] F32, norm [512]; q_layernorm [1024], kv_layernorm [512]; attn_sink [64] F32. There is NO indexer tensor in an HCA layer.

Precision boundaries of the HCA path: the compressor's kv and score projections run in bf16 inputs with an fp32 OUTPUT (out_dtype float32); state, APE, softmax, pooling and the compressor RMSNorm are fp32; the nope part goes through a bf16 round trip before FP8 quantisation while the rope part is rotated in fp32 and rounded once; the RoPE cos/sin cache is fp32; q and kv rotations are computed in fp32 and rounded to the model dtype (per the XPU Triton reference of the fused CUDA kernel); the sink is fp32; the output of attention is model dtype and the inverse-rotated output is block-FP8 quantised only when wo_a stays FP8 (128x128 block-FP8 checkpoints).
